source_title: "Popping" the SSE4.2 requirement in Windows 11, and X'ing out the NX bit requirement in Windows 10. - GitHub
source_excerpt:
This is an experimental patcher that patches various Windows versions to boot on unsupported hardware.
It started as a patcher that allowed CPUs with POPCNT, but without SSE4.2 (such as the AMD Phenom and K10 lines of CPUs) to boot Windows 11 24H2 and beyond. The project now also supports patching Windows 10's NX bit requirement as well, allowing users to install the latest version of Windows 10 on systems as old as the year 2000.
What? Windows 11 needs that. This is impossible!
Yes and no. While Windows 11 checks for both POPCNT and SSE4.2, it does not actually need SSE4.2 for 99% of its files, with only a few exceptions that can be worked around (read on). To enforce this, Microsoft uses the undocumented RtlDetectProcessorFeatures function and checks for requirements by reading data from .rdata . In kernel 26100.7171, this is at offset 00000001400088C0 and has the bytes 01 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 10 00 02 00 00 00 0D 00 00 00 in IDA. To defeat this, we simply flip that 0D to a 0C , telling Windows to effectively skip the check and continue booting.
It technically does and hardcodes it plentifully, but due to how NX works, there is no reason Microsoft could not have made it optional. NX bit (bit 63) is essentially a "never execute this in memory" flag designed to avoid executing data as executable code in memory. It is not an instruction like POPCNT and others are.
While it is an instrumental part of modern system security (see TwilightHack for the Nintendo Wii for what happens without it), using it on systems without it is considered invalid, as the original PAE specification marked bit 63 as "reserved". Due to this, getting Windows 10 to work required manually patching every call site that hardcoded it (winload, ntoskrnl, hal/halmacpi), since simply patching the requirement check and using nx AlwaysOff was far from enough.
While this sounds virtually impossible on the surface, the amount of WRMSRs and bit 63 writes become much more centralized once you realize that only ring 0 on x86 systems can utilize it, meaning the entirety of userspace (smss, ntdll, everything users run) will just work once all the low-level code is patched. Indeed, once Windows 10 booted—everything just worked.
If running from source, Python 3.7+ with pefile : pip install pefile
Windows ADK (Deployment Tools) for oscdimg.exe . It will be automatically downloaded if missing.
(If patching Windows 11 and lack SSE4.1) A copy of WindowsCodecs.dll (64-bit) and msxml6.dll (both 64-bit and 32-bit) extracted from Windows 11 23H2 placed into the blobs/ directory (see "Why do I need DLLs?" below). The 32-bit WOW64 variant of msxml6.dll must be renamed to "msxml6_wow64.dll".
1. Build a Full Patched ISO (Recommended)
Substitute python winpopbit.py with winpopbit.exe if running from a release build.

This command will automatically request Administrator elevation to manage WIM mounts and offline registry hives.
If you only need to patch individual binaries directly (e.g. for testing or Windows PE):
Patch the NT Kernel ( ntoskrnl.exe ): python winpopbit.py patch kernel_sse42 -i path \t o \n toskrnl.exe -o path \t o \n toskrnl_patched.exe
Patch the Boot Loader ( winload.efi / winload.exe ): python winpopbit.py patch winload -i path \t o \w inload.exe -o path \t o \w inload_patched.exe
Patch the Provisioning Tool ( provtool.exe ): python winpopbit.py patch provtool_exit -i path \t o \p rovtool.exe -o path \t o \p rovtool_patched.exe
Patch the NT Kernel ( ntoskrnl.exe ): python winpopbit.py patch kernel_nx -i path \t o \n toskrnl.exe -o path \t o \n toskrnl_patched.exe
Patch the Boot Loader ( winload.efi / winload.exe ): python winpopbit.py patch winload_nx -i path \t o \w inload.exe -o path \t o \w inload_patched.exe
Patch the HAL ( hal.dll / halmacpi.dll ): python winpopbit.py patch hal_nx -i path \t o \h al.dll -o path \t o \h al_patched.dll
If -o is omitted, the input binary will be modified and overwritten in-place.
This patcher is deprecated and completely lacks support for the new NX patches. You probably want to use the Python script instead for PE.
This can be found in the patcher_legacy folder of this repository. It's a standard Win32 app that should execute on basically anything that can run a Win32 executable.
The one exception to this requirement is some VIA U3xxx CPUs, since they have SSE4.1. For these, a separate badblobs configuration file is provided and can be used with the -c flag.
For some reason, Microsoft compiled WindowsCodecs.dll and msxml6.dll with SSE4.1 instructions ( PMOVSXBW and PMOVZXBW ). If you do not replace WindowsCodecs.dll , Windows Setup will crash and restart when attempting to execute it. Even if you deploy the WIM manually, Windows will later enter Automatic Recovery as it tries to execute setup.exe again to finish installing. Likewise, skipping msxml6.dll will cause Windows to appear to install, but later fail to register any AppX package, resulting in "Why did my PC restart?" and a very broken install that can't even start explorer. For these reasons, replacing these files with their 23H2 versions in blobs/ is required.
Customizing Blobs and BCD ( badblobs.xml )
WinPOPBit tracks problematic binaries and boot configurations using badblobs.xml . Each entry defines target paths and actions ( patch , replace , ignore ). You can customize or add replacement blobs by editing badblobs.xml .
Additionally, the section allows configuring which bcdedit commands are executed against both the BIOS ( boot\bcd ) and UEFI ( efi\microsoft\boot\bcd ) BCD stores on the installation media:
AGP GPUs will not work by default. See this post on the drivers Discussion thread for a solution.
For NX patching, you have to manually set nx AlwaysOff to avoid a MEMORY_MANAGEMENT bluescreen on Northwood and Willamette, and nointegritychecks Yes to fix booting after install.
Certain Nvidia nForce chipsets hang on boot on Windows 11. Needs further investigation.
Intel Core 2 CPUs are not currently supported on Windows 11. These lack POPCNT, which is used heavily.
This whole thing is experimental. Please file any bugs or quirks you find in the Issues tab.
Works on an Intel Pentium 4 Northwood from 2002!
You can review Patching and Installing Windows 11 26H2 Walkthrough for guidance on how to practically patch and install Windows 11 on an unsupported system.
